Thus all but one evaluation are >=kappa*actualheight for a computable normalized pair separation kappa. When two primitive linears are exceptionally small at the same root, their integer 2x2 determinant must vanish, so at most one normalized primitive line survives per root. Very small evaluation at a bounded remaining root may force x comparable to actual height up to that root's modulus. These are leads, not reviewed lemmas. A valid weaker theorem with explicit missing condition is preferable to an unsupported uniform bound.

Avoid conflating field selection, fixed-N ordinary base, random-N average and special families. State exact rational N-only certificate and polynomial construction/verification costs. Supplied approximate root locations are not an oracle; certified disks or reviewed root isolation can be used with unknown outcomes. No factor or order advice.

If small-height strata account for most candidates, acknowledge their smaller rational norm and describe what genuinely different joint-yield model would be needed; do not apply the full-height smoothness law as an unconditional bound. Zero norms, f reducibility/squarefreeness, signs/normalization, duplicates and prime-ideal completion remain separate. A conditional upper supply obstruction does not prove factoring hardness or general field-selection failure.

No numerical root sample, parameter sweep or finite experiment is requested or preregistered; work analytically and check primary sources only for specific used theorems.
